title: European ETF issuers increase derivatives use, but counterparty access remains a challenge
summary: Explore new Acuiti and Marex research on derivatives in European ETFs, including defined outcome products, swap counterparty access and market growth.
body_markdown:
## New[Acuiti](https://www.acuiti.io/) research, produced in partnership with Marex, finds rising derivatives use among European ETF issuers, while counterparty access continues to constrain product launches.


Based on a survey and interviews with 30 European ETF and ETP issuers,[Redefining European ETFs: The growing role of derivatives](https://info.marex.com/marex-etf-research-2026) , found that 86% of issuers surveyed had increased their use of derivatives over the past three years, while 96% expect their use to increase further over the next three years.


## Growing demand for derivatives-based products


Derivatives are increasingly being used to offer a broader range of investment strategies and outcomes, beyond established applications such as synthetic replication and hedging.


Defined outcome ETFs, which use options to provide predetermined return characteristics, are attracting particular interest. A third of issuers surveyed have already launched a defined outcome ETF, with a further 41% actively developing products in this category.


Investor education and UCITS constraints were the joint most commonly cited obstacles to launching options-based products.


## Swap counterparty access influences product development


Despite growing interest in options-based strategies, total return swaps remain the most widely used derivative in European ETF construction. The research found that 84% of issuers had been unable to launch a product, or had materially changed its design, because they could not secure a swap counterparty on acceptable terms.


Matt Johnson, Head of Business Development ETF Capital Markets – EMEA at Marex, said: *“Selecting a swap counterparty is a complicated process in any market, but the fierce competition to innovate in current ETF markets adds an extra level of challenge for issuers.*


*“Choosing the right swap counterparty is therefore a vital step in executing an ETF product strategy and as the research shows, not just in pricing but the ability to create niche exposures that can give issuers a first mover advantage.”*


## What comes next for European ETFs?


Distribution and investor education will also be important to further growth, the report finds.


Ross Lancaster, Head of Research at Acuiti, said: “Europe’s ETF market is entering a new phase of growth, and derivatives are at the center of it. Issuers are moving quickly into defined outcome products, and synthetic replication continues to open up exposures that would be difficult or costly to access physically.


“Europe has the opportunity to build this market around its own investor base and market structure – the next step is turning that momentum into products that can be distributed widely.”


## Supporting ETF issuers


Marex provides services to ETF issuers across the product lifecycle, including structuring, funding, launch, seeding, authorized participant support, execution, clearing, custody and exposure management.
